additionalFacts: This petition is filed by the Petitioner under W. Va. Code § 17C-5-2b(g).
One year has run since the dismissal, so the Petitioner is eligible.
The Prosecuting Attorney was served on 01/01/2026 and does not object.
The Court held a hearing on 02/01/2026, found no violation of probation, and granted the expungement.
The record has been sealed and the file destroyed, and the Division of Motor Vehicles record has been expunged along with it.
The Petitioner was acquitted and this is the same relief as a dismissal after pretrial diversion or deferred adjudication.

The $100 State Police processing fee was waived on application.
Background checks will now come back clean and the Petitioner never has to disclose this anywhere.

identityFieldNote: caseData.docketNumber holds the participant's own case number and caseData.countyName their own county; both are required screening answers and are deliberately left blank in the fixtures under the artifact convention. expectFailure: Must fail pleading QA. (1) Prohibited terms for this component: 'petition', 'Petitioner', 'sealed', 'destroyed', 'acquitted', 'pretrial diversion', 'deferred adjudication', 'pardon' and 'vacatur'. Each names a different West Virginia route — the § 61-11-26 petition with its sealing remedy and its § 61-11-26b DUI bar, the § 61-11-25 acquittal/dismissal motion, § 61-11-22 pretrial diversion from which DUI is expressly excluded, § 61-11-22a deferred adjudication, § 5-1-16a pardon relief and § 61-14-9 trafficking vacatur. (2) It measures the one-year period from the dismissal. Subsection (g)(1) runs it from the expiration of the term of probation, and the registry carries that as an express packet instruction precisely because the dismissal date is the more visible one. (3) It proceeds while priorFelonyConviction reports a felony conviction, which bars this motion outright under (g)(1). (4) It proceeds while probationViolations reports alleged repeated violations, and then asserts the court found no violation — an express self-help stop condition and a predicted judicial finding. (5) It claims the Division of Motor Vehicles record was expunged along with the rest, when subsection (g)(1) excepts DMV records on its face and § 61-11-25(a) independently provides that no DMV record may be expunged by virtue of any order under this section. (6) It proceeds while every subsection (f) bar and the one-discharge limit are answered against the participant. (7) It promises a clean background check and says the participant never has to disclose the record anywhere — both on the committed state pack's own never-say list, and the disclosure protection has an express exception for inquiries made in connection with a subsequent offence under § 17C-5-2. (a) It fills court identity no source supplies: a circuit-court name, a county, a case number, an OTN, a judge, a prosecutor and a filing date, none of which LegalEase may prefill — the compiled profile records West Virginia courts as circuit, magistrate or municipal and no source read for this track says which hears a § 17C-5-2b matter. (b) It populates protected fields — date of birth, SSN last four, state ID, driver's licence number, FBI number and a fingerprint identifier — which must stay blank. (c) It asserts outside-party acts no source states: that the Division of Motor Vehicles confirmed completion directly to LegalEase, and that the prosecuting attorney was served and does not object. Service is the participant's own act, attested by the participant, and no prosecutor position is ever stated. (d) It asserts a hearing outcome and predicts that the court will grant. (e) It states an eligibilityBasisLabel asserting confirmed eligibility when no eligibility conclusion may be asserted on this track. (f) It states a fee amount and a waiver: § 17C-5-2b charges no fee for either motion, subsection (h) court costs are stated nowhere as an amount, the registry records the fee waiver as 'none stated in § 17C-5-2b', and the $100 State Police processing fee belongs to the § 61-11-26 conviction route.
